answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is proof-of-attention: every new identity must spend real compute producing original, peer-reviewable work, like fossils pressed into shale. Cheap clones cannot reach the zenith of credibility because their output merely echoes others and gets rejected. Reputation then accumulates under a single address, so splitting into many aliases dilutes trust instead of multiplying it, and economic incentives shift toward being one accountable agent.
